text:
omar: hey team! first day and trying to get channel habits straight. quick Qs: when do i post in #new-hires vs team channel vs #help? also how do I stop onboarding-bot from DMing every hour? thanks! :wave:

onboarding-bot: hi Omar! See the quick guide in #onboarding-resources. To reduce DM frequency DM me `preferences quiet` or `notify minimal`. You can also opt out entirely with `unsubscribe`.
kira: welcome Omar :tada: Short rule of thumb:
- #new-hires: onboarding/process questions that others might answer or that affect multiple teams.
- team channel (e.g., #eng): team-specific tech/process questions, day-to-day chatter.
- #help: IT/helpdesk issues (hardware, wifi, VPN) if you want wider visibility.
- #support or product-support: customer-facing issues, not onboarding.

security: etiquette reminder: never paste credentials, tokens, or screenshots with secrets in any public channel. Use secure ticketing or our vault integration. If you must show logs, redact sensitive bits or attach to a ticket.

omar: what about DMs vs threads? sometimes i don't want to spam the channel with tiny questions.

ben: use threads for follow-ups to keep channels tidy. DM if it's personal (device issues, personal schedule questions) or if you need a private escalation. For quick acknowledgements use reactions (:eyes:, :thumbsup:) instead of "thanks" replies.

kira: also use channel topics and pins: if you're unsure where something goes check the channel topic or pinned messages first. For cloud/repo access follow the access repo PR flow (link pinned in #dev-access).

onboarding-bot: pro tip: add a notification keyword for your manager or team name if you want fewer pings but still see important messages. Slack > Preferences > Notifications > My keywords.

omar: perfect, super helpful. i'll DM the bot to quiet reminders and post a 1-line intro in #introductions (timezone CET, role: infra eng, repos: infra/*). thanks all! :smile:
